methodology: Bounded first-pass screening of Qur'an 4:51–60 using published Arabic/English Qur'an and Sefaria Hebrew/2023 Revised JPS for Deuteronomy 16:18–20. Similarity is not literary dependence. No critical apparatus or manuscript collation; staged only.

verses.summary: Critique of recipients of scripture believing in jibt and taghut and praising another group's guidance
Question of a share in sovereignty and refusal to give even a small amount
Envy regarding God's favor; Abraham's family given scripture, wisdom and kingdom
Some accepted and others turned away; warning of Gehenna
Fire punishment and renewal of skins in eschatological judgment
Reward of believers: gardens, purified spouses and shade
Return trusts to their owners and judge fairly between people
Obey God, messenger and authorities; refer disputes to God and messenger
Critique of claimed believers seeking judgment from taghut despite injunction to reject it
Claimants to belief in earlier and present revelation seeking arbitration by taghut

staged_candidates.relationship: shared judicial-justice norm; not direct narrative parallel
staged_candidates.similarity: Both command just judgment; Deuteronomy prescribes impartial magistrates and condemns bribery, while Qur'an 4:58 also orders the return of entrusted property.
staged_candidates.difference: Deuteronomy locates magistrates in Israelite settlements and connects justice with residence in the land; Qur'an 4:58 does not prescribe that institution or mention the land.
